headline: South Asia: Automating death: Israel’s AI-powered genocide in Gaza
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Automating death: Israel’s AI-powered genocide in Gaza.
- Asia: Russia batters Ukraine’s power facilities amid Kyiv’s growing strain with US.
- Australia: Zelenskyy says partners not warning Ukraine of incoming ballistic missiles.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Army eyes changes to emergency war gear stocks amid review.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: Army eyes changes to emergency war gear stocks amid review.
The Army is nearing decisions on changes to make to its own emergency stockpiles.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Anduril reveals family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles.
The interceptor family was built to address threats across the air-and-missile defense spectrum, while aiming to come at a fraction of the cost of others.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: US Army to stand up command for unmanned and autonomous warfare.
An Oct. 1 memo directs the Army vice chief of staff to establish the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, or FASCOM.
The Caribbean - bottom line: IC wants probe of single-source contracts.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: IC wants probe of single-source contracts.
Declaring that competition was the exception in the awarding of government contracts last year, Kevon Stephenson, director of investigation at the Integrity Commission, says in 2025, single-source procurement, including emergency contracting, accounted for 69.2 per cent of contracts by number and 27.3 per cent by value. By contrast, open competitive bidding accounted for 4.1 per cent of contracts by number. In a special report to Parliament, Stephenson highlighted that single-source procurement has accounted for about two-thirds of contracts in every year since 2017.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: TCN CAUTION - Gov’t urged to weigh legal liabilities as 22 deported foreigners arrive under US deal.
The arrival of 22 Latin American and European migrants at Norman Manley International Airport under the controversial third county nationals agreement (TCN) has triggered a warning from one political analyst that Jamaica could face legal liabilities. University of the West Indies lecturer in the Department of Government Damion Gordon said the Holness administration must ensure openness, and evaluate its responsibilities regarding the agreement.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Three called to Inner Bar as Chief Justice urges leadership, service.
Three members of Jamaica’s legal profession – Deputy Solicitor General Lisa White, Director of Public Prosecutions Claudette Thompson and veteran attorney Oswest Senior-Smith – have been called to the Inner Bar, with Chief Justice Bryan Sykes urging them to use their elevation to strengthen the justice system and uphold the rule of law. Addressing the ceremony on Tuesday morning, Sykes reminded the newly appointed King’s Counsel (KC) that the honour was not simply a reward for past achievements but an obligation to serve the courts, the legal profession, and the country.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: JHTA fears winter season gridlock as MoBay roadworks lag.
WESTERN BUREAU: The Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association (JHTA) is warning that worsening traffic congestion in Montego Bay threatens to disrupt the winter tourist season as major roadworks remain unfinished. JHTA Area Chapter Chairman Kerry-Ann Quallo-Casserly has expressed growing frustration over delays in completing Phase One of the Montego Bay Perimeter Road project, which was originally scheduled for completion in June, subsequently pushed back to September, and remains unfinished in October.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

[African Arguments] The peace agreement between Congo and Rwanda contains one promise about justice: that no fighter will be taken into the Congolese army until someone has checked whether they committed atrocities. The last time Congo skipped that check, the soldiers it absorbed went on to start the war now being negotiated. The check is not happening this time either.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Automating death: Israel’s AI-powered genocide in Gaza.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Automating death: Israel’s AI-powered genocide in Gaza.
On February 29, 2024, Israeli forces fired at civilians as they gathered around an aid convoy. At least 115 people were killed in what has since become known as the ‘Flour Massacre’. Survivors recalled the involvement of armed tanks and quadcopters. “When the aid entered, the tank and quadcopter started firing at the people gathered, the people who went to get food for themselves and their children. They started shooting at them,” Mahmoud Ahmad, a Gaza resident, told Reuters shortly after the incident.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Makkah Alliance secretary general meets PM Shehbaz, briefs premier on defence cooperation.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday met the newly appointed secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, and was briefed on the strategy to promote “defence and strategic cooperation” under the pact, state-run Radio Pakistan reported. Mahmood was appointed as the first secretary general of the defence alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month. The agreement — signed on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, Jerusalem Post, Yonhap News Agency, just now: Houthis warn of ‘painful’ response as Saudis strike Yemen fuel sites.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: US may have ‘gone too far’ in targeting Iran leaders.
OHIO: US President Donald Trump said that the United States “might have gone too far” in targeting Iran’s leadership. “We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don’t know who the hell we’re dealing with any more,” he said during a campaign rally in Ohio, according to Middle East Eye. “Nobody wants to be the president of Iran,” he added, claiming that potential candidates did not want to take up the position. Trump made this remark despite Masoud Pezeshkian being Iran’s president since July 2024.

Daljeet was reportedly beaten for nearly an hour before being locked in a room. His condition worsened after returning home, leading to his hospitalization and subsequent death.
